markdown_report:
**Proposed direction: calibrated candidate-depth diagnostics for the existing NextItNet models.** At 10% progress, retain this feasible extension, but distinguish mathematically inevitable competition effects from informative ranking differences. No validation improvement is claimed.

**Insights from the starting point**

1. Electronics’ sampled negative-win rate is 12.27%, versus 0.96% for CDs_and_Vinyl. This motivates investigation; raw margins remain score-scale dependent.
2. Alignment scores of 0.507–0.523 imply near-zero mean cosine similarity. They do not establish useful geometry or exclude other representation failures.
3. Existing padding, causality and perturbation controls support a small ranking extension. Training-prefix measurements assess fit, not generalization or current intent.

**Insights from related work**

1. [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse comparisons. Nested candidate expansion necessarily worsens or preserves rank; declining diagnostic HR alone therefore reveals no unexpected weakness.
2. [Negative-sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) motivates popularity strata. Repeated draws quantify candidate randomness without removing sampling bias.
3. [Patching methodology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) motivates controlled comparisons. [Temporal-leakage research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11060) additionally cautions that retrospective training-prefix exclusions are not prospective information.

**Framework and research directions**

| Direction | Existing evidence | Missing measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Ranking competition | Single-negative margins | Rank distribution and expected sampling effects |
| Failure localization | Category aggregates | Frequency, length and coverage strata |
| Temporal mechanism | History perturbations | Block-specific recovery and shortcut checks |

**Candidate ideas**

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Calibrated candidate-depth audit — 4/6/4.** Originality: controlled integration, but established sampling theory. Potential: clarifies ranking limitations, but in-sample depth decline cannot establish generalization. Difficulty: scoring hooks help, but ties, eligibility and uncertainty require care. References: Krichene–Rendle; negative-sampling research.
- **Frequency-stratified training negatives — 3/7/4.** Originality: useful adaptation, but standard machinery. Potential: may improve confusing comparisons, but can increase false negatives or popularity shortcuts. Difficulty: compact sampler change, but validation remains necessary. Reference: negative-sampling research.
- **Residual-block activation recovery — 6/7/7.** Originality: transfers patching to NextItNet, but established methodology. Potential: localizes computation, but recovery need not improve recommendations. Difficulty: hooks help, but corruption validity and distributed effects complicate interpretation. Reference: patching methodology.

**Selected algorithm**

Freeze each category’s single checkpoint. Select deterministic training-prefix targets and nested uniform sets of 99, 499 and 999 unique negatives where eligible. Report rank, diagnostic hit rate, positive-minus-tenth-negative margin, frequency/length strata and eligibility. Use identical users across paired depths.

For an eligible pool of size N containing M negatives preceding the target under fixed tie-breaking, X~Hypergeometric(N,M,m), sampled rank=1+X and expected hit rate=P(X≤9). Compute M through optional chunked full-pool scoring on a bounded audit subset. This describes sampling effects, not a universal degradation curve or significance test for model quality.

Bootstrap users conditional on candidates; report repeated-draw variability separately. Label results in-sample and exclusions retrospective. Popularity, shuffled-history and truncated-history controls probe shortcuts without proving memorization. Compare permitted host validation summaries only when supplied. Preserve diagnostic entry points, RNG/modes, final-nonpadding readout, routing and the fixed macro validation HR@10 selection criterion.

idea.description: Extend the existing padding-aware NextItNet diagnostic adapter with a calibrated, paired candidate-depth audit. Use fixed training-prefix targets, nested unique-negative sets and optional exact eligible-pool ranks to separate inevitable competition effects from descriptive ranking differences. Retain one independently trained checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Electronics has weaker measured sampled training separation than the other categories, while the reported angular alignment does not indicate strong global directional collapse. Candidate-depth measurements can characterize fitted ranking behavior, but deterioration under nested expansion is mathematically expected and cannot itself establish a model defect. The audit must distinguish training fit, candidate randomness, popularity dependence and host validation performance. It cannot infer compatibility, saturation, current intent or simulator traits from unavailable evidence.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), preserving all existing probes. Access the actual network through view.model and score through view.log2feats and view.predict_score; preserve item_emb, user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility. Use only permitted training histories and mapped real training items. Do not access held-out labels to construct pools. Define one endpoint per sampled user: prefix=training_history[:-1], target=training_history[-1], requiring at least two interactions. Uniformly sample at most 200 eligible users per category without replacement using local deterministic generators seeded from 42 and stable category indices; sort user IDs before sampling and record selected IDs and cutoffs. This endpoint may have been optimized during training and must be labeled in-sample. Left-pad/truncate using the trained model's sequence length and select the largest nonzero input index, never count-1; skip empty prefixes. Define the negative pool as all real training item IDs excluding the target and every item in that user's permitted training history. Excluding later training interactions relative to the prefix is retrospective hindsight, not a prospective policy. Record repeated-target status before exclusion. Draw one uniform ordered pool without replacement and take nested prefixes of lengths 99, 499 and 999. Use ten independent repetitions with deterministic local seeds, sharing each repetition across depths. Report unavailable depths and reasons when pools are too small. Report both depth-specific summaries and paired comparisons restricted to users eligible at every compared depth. Break score ties consistently by ascending item ID. Compute positive rank, hit-at-10 and the raw margin against the tenth highest-scoring negative; the margin is score-scale dependent. Define frequency from all permitted training interactions: head=top 20% of real items by frequency, middle=next 30%, tail=remaining items, with item-ID tie-breaking; define prefix-length bins 1–5, 6–20 and above 20 before truncation. Report bin counts, user coverage and repeated-target status. On at most 50 deterministically selected audit users per category, optionally score the full eligible pool in chunks, streaming the count M of negatives that precede the target and retaining only top scores. With pool size N and sample depth m, use scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf(9, N, M, m) for the exact conditional expected diagnostic HR@10; expected sampled rank is 1+m*M/N. The eligible pool is smaller than an unrestricted catalog because of exclusions, so label this full-eligible-pool rank. The formula assumes uniform sampling without replacement and the declared tie order; it does not apply unchanged to popularity-weighted samples. Do not interpret nested monotonic decline or expected-versus-observed sampling residuals as evidence of poor generalization. Aggregate users equally within category and categories equally only when all four are available. Use 2,000 paired user-cluster bootstrap resamples conditional on one fixed candidate repetition. Separately report the standard deviation across the ten repetition-level macro summaries, and SD/sqrt(10) only as Monte Carlo standard error of their average with users and models fixed. Never count repetitions as independent users. These intervals omit training-seed and adaptive-search uncertainty. Report recommendation popularity and catalog coverage on permitted histories and reuse controlled shuffle/truncation probes as descriptive shortcut checks; none alone proves memorization or exposure bias. Host validation summaries or strata may be compared only if supplied through the permitted interface; do not modify the evaluator or silently compute unavailable validation results. Preserve all module modes and Python/NumPy/Torch/CUDA RNG states, bound scoring chunks and audit counts, and report elapsed diagnostic cost. Keep training, predictor behavior, checkpoints and dataset routing unchanged. Any later training proposal must retain NextItNet, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts and synchronized predictor writing. No auxiliary fitted scorer, checkpoint reuse, independent score fusion or ensemble is allowed.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        with preserve_module_modes_and_rng(self.view.model):
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                result = run_existing_probes(train_loader)
                users = deterministic_sorted_user_sample(max_users=200, seed=42)
                records, coverage, exact = [], [], []
                for user in users:
                    history = permitted_training_history(user)
                    if len(history) < 2:
                        record_exclusion(coverage, user, 'no training prefix')
                        continue
                    prefix, target = history[:-1], history[-1]
                    sequence = left_pad_and_truncate(prefix, trained_sequence_length)
                    endpoint = largest_nonzero_index(sequence)
                    if endpoint is None:
                        continue
                    features = self.view.log2feats(sequence[None, :])
                    feature = features[0, endpoint]
                    pool = sorted(real_training_items - set(history) - {target})
                    positive_score = score_one(self.view, feature, target)
                    strata = fixed_training_frequency_length_and_repeat_strata(prefix, target)
                    if user in deterministic_exact_rank_subset(users, maximum=50):
                        M = stream_count_preceding_target(
                            self.view, feature, pool, positive_score,
                            tie_break='ascending item ID', chunk_size=4096)
                        N = len(pool)
                        exact.append({user, N, M, full_eligible_rank: 1 + M,
                                      expected_hits: {m: hypergeom_cdf(9, N, M, m)
                                                      for m in (99, 499, 999) if m <= N}})
                    for repetition in range(10):
                        negatives = uniform_ordered_sample_without_replacement(
                            pool, maximum=999,
                            local_seed=stable_seed(42, category_index, user, repetition))
                        scores = score_in_chunks(self.view, feature, negatives, chunk_size=4096)
                        for depth in (99, 499, 999):
                            if len(negatives) < depth:
                                record_unavailable(coverage, user, repetition, depth,
                                                   'insufficient unique negatives')
                                continue
                            rank = 1 + count_preceding_target(
                                negatives[:depth], scores[:depth], target, positive_score,
                                tie_break='ascending item ID')
                            records.append({user, repetition, depth, rank,
                                            diagnostic_hit_at_10: rank <= 10,
                                            margin_to_tenth_negative:
                                                positive_score - tenth_largest(scores[:depth]),
                                            strata})
                check_nested_rank_monotonicity(records)
                result.update(summarize_depths_and_common_eligible_users(records, coverage))
                result.update(paired_user_bootstrap(records, fixed_repetition=0,
                                                    resamples=2000, local_seed=42))
                result.update(candidate_repetition_variability(records))
                result.update(exact_sampling_expectations(exact))
                result.update(permitted_history_popularity_coverage_and_existing_controls())
                return {'metrics': result,
                        'metric_definitions': definitions_with_counts_ties_exclusions_costs_and_limits()}

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return build_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis['metrics'], raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        constraints='In-sample exploratory diagnostics; nested decline is expected; '
                    'no inferred current intent, causal mechanism or validation gains; '
                    'one NextItNet checkpoint per category; unavailable evidence stays unknown.')

originality.positive: Combines exact sampling expectations, paired candidate sets and existing NextItNet controls in a reproducible task-specific diagnostic adapter.
originality.negative: Hypergeometric sampling theory, popularity strata and clustered uncertainty are established methods; the contribution is integration rather than a new estimator.

future_potential.positive: Can prevent misleading interpretations and identify descriptive ranking patterns that motivate narrowly targeted training experiments.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix audits may largely reflect memorization, and expected candidate-depth degradation provides limited actionable evidence about held-out improvement.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses ModelView and requires no architecture, checkpoint or inference changes; exact ranks can be computed with bounded memory.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible tie handling, retrospective exclusions, paired eligibility, exact-rank subsets and separate uncertainty estimates require more care than a basic sampling loop.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can reverse model comparisons, including in expectation.
Motivates distinguishing the pinned sampled benchmark from full-eligible-pool ranking.
limitations: Does not establish that candidate-depth diagnostics predict validation improvement for these NextItNet models.
Does not justify replacing the pinned evaluator or treating repeated sampling as removal of sampling bias.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation — IJCAI Extended Abstract
contributions: Discusses sampled-rank distributions and the interpretation of sampled recommendation metrics.
Supports calibrating the proposed audit using the exact hypergeometric distribution for uniform sampling without replacement.
limitations: The audit's exclusion rules, bootstrap design and bounded exact-rank subset are task-specific adaptations.
The hypergeometric expectation requires a fixed eligible pool, fixed scores and consistent tie-breaking.

related_work.title: Evaluating Performance and Bias of Negative Sampling
contributions: Examines negative-sampling effects and performance differences across popularity bands.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal sampler for these four categories.
Popularity-stratified training performance cannot by itself distinguish preference learning from exposure-related shortcuts.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Introduces causal dilated convolutions and residual connections for sequential recommendation.
limitations: Architectural history access does not establish learned influence, current intent or generalization.
The supplied corrected backbone and final-nonpadding readout remain authoritative for implementation.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models
contributions: Shows that corruption and measurement choices affect activation-patching conclusions.
Motivates controlled interventions and explicit measurement limitations.
limitations: Provides transferable methodology rather than validated NextItNet-specific results.
Activation recovery and null perturbation effects do not independently establish recommendation quality.

related_work.title: A Critical Study on Data Leakage in Recommender System Offline Evaluation
contributions: Documents temporal leakage concerns in recommendation evaluation.
Motivates labeling retrospective training-prefix exclusions and avoiding prospective forecasting claims.
limitations: Does not authorize changes to the host splits or evaluator.
The proposed audit remains in-sample even when its negative pools use only permitted training data.

related_work.title: ClusterBootstrap
contributions: Provides methodological support for resampling subjects as clusters when observations repeat within subjects.
Motivates preserving paired depth observations within each resampled user.
limitations: The four-category paired diagnostic procedure is a proposed adaptation.
User bootstrap intervals do not capture training-seed variability, adaptive selection or all candidate-sampling uncertainty.
